newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES POLE AS WILLIAMS LEAD AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES POLE AS WILLIAMS LEAD AGAIN.

text.p: Canadian Jacques Villeneuve set a qualifying lap record and secured his fifth pole position of the season on Saturday when he outpaced his Williams team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen in qualifying for Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix.
Villeneuve, 25, sent the dust flying on the final corner with a committed effort as he clocked one minute 16.525 seconds with just three minutes of the session remaining.

It was the eighth pole of his career in Formula One and enhanced his hopes of overhauling German Michael Schumacher's four-point lead in the drivers' championship with victory in the 65-lap race on the demanding Circuit de Catalunya.

His time cut more than four seconds off last year's record pole time set by Briton Damon Hill in a Williams. It was another comprehensive demonstration of the increased speed of this year's cars as a result of the tyre war between Goodyear and Bridgestone.
Villeneuve was just two-tenths of a second faster than second-placed Frentzen, whose Spanish mother makes him the nearest thing to a local driver in the field.

Briton David Coulthard was third for McLaren ahead of Frenchman Jean Alesi in a Benetton. Mika Hakkinen of Finland was fifth in the second McLaren and Austrian Gerhard Berger sixth for Benetton, confirmation of the Anglo-Italian team's long-awaited return to form.

Michael Schumacher, in his Ferrari, was seventh-quickest, after suffering an engine failure and switching to his race car, ahead of Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan. Briton Damon Hill, the defending world champion, struggled to claim 15th place in his Arrows.

Villeneuve's achievement extended the Williams team's domination of pole position to 10 successive races -- stretching back to last August's Hungarian Grand Prix at Budapest -- on the 20th anniversary of the current team's first race, the Spanish Grand Prix of 1977 at Jarama, near Madrid.

Villeneuve said he was delighted to claim pole with his last-gasp effort after making a series of minor changes to his car during the qualifying hour. "We did a little tweak towards the end and it made the difference," he said.

"The car was just a little better and I was able to go a little quicker than Heinz-Harald but it was close. I feel the car is very good, the team is strong and we are in very good shape and feeling confident."

Asked what he would do if it rained -- a reference to the forecast wet weather for Sunday and to the Williams team's mistakes in Monaco where they ran on dry 'slick' tyres in the wet -- Villeneuve smiled as he said: "If it rains, we will go on wet tyres this time!"

Frentzen said he was disappointed but had not made any alterations to his car in the changing conditions of the session as the temperature and wind varied. He predicted a physically demanding race which could be decided by tyre strategy.

Coulthard, whose third place on the grid is his best starting position for 18 months, said that even though his McLaren was much improved in balance and performance, he could not imagine catching the Williams cars.
"But we are on good shape to finish on the podium," he said. "Tyre wear will be a vital issue and pit stops will be very important in this race."
